title: The terminal privilege sweep bricks `npm run test:fund-user` on every fresh local chain, and the comment on the failing line still claims the deployer is an authorized minter
fingerprintNote: Accepted VERBATIM as supplied by dedup. NOT recomputed by finding-manager. The fingerprint is the only collision-proof key for this record; the label L-xx/Q-xx is run-scoped and collides with run-21 and run-26 labels on this same entry point.
description: `_sweepResidualPrivileges` (DeployMocks.s.sol:1917) revokes the deployer's phUSD mint authority as the last transaction of every `npm run dev`. `script/interactions/FundTestUser.s.sol:46` calls `MockPhUSD(phUSD).mint(testUser, phUSDAmount)` inside a broadcast opened at :43 with `AddressLoader.getDefaultPrivateKey()` — anvil account #0, i.e. the deployer — and contains no `setMinter` re-grant anywhere in the file. Reproduced empirically on a fresh chain immediately after a clean `npm run dev`: `npm run test:fund-user` exits 1 with the verbatim revert `Not authorized to mint` (src/mocks/MockPhUSD.sol:48), trace tail `│   └─ ← [Revert] Not authorized to mint / └─ ← [Revert] Not authorized to mint / Error: script failed: Not authorized to mint`. The comment immediately above the failing call — `// Mint phUSD (deployer is authorized minter)` — is now false and will actively mislead whoever debugs this. An independent repo-wide consumer sweep confirms FundTestUser is the ONLY local consumer of the deployer's phUSD grant: simulate-yield.sh mints MockDola (permissionless), MintPhUSD.s.sol routes through PhusdStableMinter (own grant), FullFlowTest.s.sol uses minter.mint, and everything else targets permissionless mocks. However `script/interactions/README.md` points at `npm run test:fund-user` four times (:47, :283, :352, :383 — the last reading 'Fund test user first'), so the broken command sits inside the documented developer workflow rather than in an obscure corner. Story 079 found this, recorded it as Autonomous Decision 4 and Review Issue 1, and deliberately declined to fix it to honour its own single-file constraint; both of its validators endorsed that reading and both recommended scheduling the one-liner. Filing it here is that scheduling, not a disagreement.
impact: A documented developer-onboarding command fails on every fresh local chain with a revert that points at the token rather than at the deploy script that removed the grant. No asset, availability or value impact — chain 31337 mock token, published key.
attackPath: 1. Not applicable — no adversary. Reproduction path instead:
2. `npm run clean:local && npm run dev` on a fresh anvil; `_sweepResidualPrivileges` broadcasts `MockPhUSD.setMinter(deployer, false)` as transaction [393] of 394 — the last in the bundle.

3. `npm run test:fund-user` opens a broadcast with `AddressLoader.getDefaultPrivateKey()` (anvil #0 = the deployer) at FundTestUser.s.sol:43 and calls `MockPhUSD.mint` at :46 with no `setMinter` re-grant anywhere in the file.
4. Revert `Not authorized to mint`; exit 1. Reproduced empirically — evidence/legA-armed-10-fund-user-regression.log.
recommendation: Add the one-line self-grant inside FundTestUser.s.sol, immediately after `vm.startBroadcast(deployerKey);` at :43 and before the mint at :46 — `MockPhUSD(phUSD).setMinter(deployer, true);` — since the deployer remains the token owner after the sweep. Update the now-false comment at :45 to say the script grants itself the right rather than assuming it. Prefer the self-grant over re-exempting the deployer in the sweep: the sweep's declarative end-state ACL is the more valuable artifact and should not be weakened to accommodate a utility script. Optionally symmetric: revoke again before `vm.stopBroadcast()` so the utility leaves the ACL as it found it.
severityRationale: C4 High requires assets stolen/lost/compromised — structurally impossible here (mock token, disposable chain, published key). C4 Medium requires protocol function or availability impact, or a value leak: a developer utility on chain 31337 is neither the protocol's function nor its availability, and no value moves. That lands it in QA/Low, and within that band it is a LOW rather than a bare QA note on two grounds: (i) it is a shipped, reproducible break of a command the project's own README instructs developers to run, introduced by the change under audit, so it has a real cost that recurs for every developer on every fresh chain; (ii) the in-source comment at the failing line now states the opposite of the truth, which converts a seconds-long fix into a misdirected debugging session — a comment that confidently asserts a false precondition is an aggravator within the band, not a neutral. Not raised further: the consumer sweep bounds the damage at exactly one dependent script.
severityRationaleAsProposed: Proposed Low. A developer-utility script on a disposable mock chain is broken — no assets, no protocol availability, no value leak. It is above QA because it is a shipped, reproducible break of a command the project's own README instructs developers to run, introduced by this change; and because the in-source comment on the failing line now asserts the opposite of the truth, which is what makes it cost time rather than seconds. Not raised further: the consumer sweep confirms exactly one dependent.

classification.assetImpact: None. Chain 31337, mock ERC-20 (MockPhUSD), deployer key published in Foundry's own documentation. No protocol asset, no user funds, no mainnet state is reachable from this closure.
classification.whatActuallyBreaks: `npm run test:fund-user` — a command `script/interactions/README.md` points at four times, the last reading 'Fund test user first' — exits 1 on every fresh local chain with `Not authorized to mint` (MockPhUSD.sol:48). The revert names the token, not the deploy script that removed the grant, and the comment on the failing line (`FundTestUser.s.sol:45`: `// Mint phUSD (deployer is authorized minter)`) now asserts the exact opposite of the truth, so the shortest honest debugging path runs through a false signpost.
classification.whatAnAttackerGains: Nothing. There is no attacker in this finding. The affected party is a developer following the project's own documented onboarding workflow, and the cost is time.
attackPath: 1. Not applicable — no adversary. Reproduction path instead:
2. `npm run clean:local && npm run dev` on a fresh anvil; `_sweepResidualPrivileges` broadcasts `MockPhUSD.setMinter(deployer, false)` as transaction [393] of 394 — the last in the bundle.

3. `npm run test:fund-user` opens a broadcast with `AddressLoader.getDefaultPrivateKey()` (anvil #0 = the deployer) at FundTestUser.s.sol:43 and calls `MockPhUSD.mint` at :46 with no `setMinter` re-grant anywhere in the file.
4. Revert `Not authorized to mint`; exit 1. Reproduced empirically — evidence/legA-armed-10-fund-user-regression.log.
classification.likelihood: certain — unconditional on every fresh local chain, no special input, no owner action, no race. Blast radius is bounded by the consumer sweep: FundTestUser is the ONLY local consumer of the deployer's phUSD grant (simulate-yield.sh mints permissionless MockDola; MintPhUSD.s.sol routes through PhusdStableMinter's own grant; FullFlowTest.s.sol uses minter.mint).
classification.assumptions: That a developer runs the documented command on a chain built by the documented command. No further assumption.

escalationTrigger: Raise to a QA-to-Low-boundary re-weigh only in the reverse direction is not needed; the trigger for raising ABOVE Low is: if any FURTHER consumer of the deployer's phUSD grant is added (or found) that sits on the mainnet or promotion-ready side rather than chain 31337, or if the same sweep pattern is mirrored into a mainnet script where the revoked grant is needed by a subsequent live step. Either would move the harm axis off the disposable chain and out of Low.
law3: NOT a Law-3 suppression and NOT an owner-malice vector. No owner action is involved at all — the break is unconditional on every run. Nor is it an owner footgun: nobody configured anything. It is straightforward collateral from a code change.

poc.reason: C4 requires a coded PoC for High/Medium only. Severity here is low.
